definitions.explanation: A small amount or number; used to emphasize how small or limited something is.
Very small in degree or amount.

examples.japanese: {僅|わず}か{五分|ごふん}で{着|つ}いた。
examples.english: I arrived in just five minutes.

examples.japanese: {残|のこ}りは{僅|わず}か{三人|さんにん}だけだった。
{彼|かれ}は{僅|わず}か{二年|にねん}で{日本語|にほんご}を{話|はな}せるようになった。
examples.english: He became able to speak Japanese in just two years.

examples.japanese: {気温|きおん}が{僅|わず}かに{上|あ}がった。
{僅|わず}かな{望|のぞ}みを{捨|す}てずに{最後|さいご}まで{努力|どりょく}した。
examples.english: Without giving up the slightest hope, I kept trying until the end.

notes:
{僅|わず}か emphasizes how small, few, or slight something is. Slightly formal in tone.

FORMS:
- {僅|わず}か + number: only/just ~ ({僅|わず}か{三人|さんにん} — only three people)
- {僅|わず}かな + noun: a slight ~ ({僅|わず}かな{差|さ} — a slight difference)
- {僅|わず}かに + verb: slightly ({僅|わず}かに{動|うご}く — move slightly)

COMMON PATTERNS:
- {僅|わず}か〜だけ: only ~, just ~
- {僅|わず}かな{望|のぞ}み: a slim hope
- {僅|わず}かに{残|のこ}る: to barely remain

CONTRAST:
- {僅|わず}か: emphasizes smallness (slightly formal)
- たった: only, just (casual, emphatic)
- ほんの: just a little (modest, softening)
- わずかに differs from {少|すこ}し in being more formal and emphasizing the minimality
